claims.quote: Notebook — margin: morphine x3 taken from pharmacy; medkit now lists: 3 morphine vials, 1 tourniquet, 2 antibiotic packets.

As an EMT trainee she doesn't have the legal right to open the controlled cabinet.
Lina wedged the pickaxe handle into the lock and Dan rammed the door. It snapped with a sound like breaking a promise.

There were three of them tucked into the rooms and the hallway when we came through the door — one on a gurney clutching at a sheet, one hunched behind the nurses' station, and another that came out of a supply closet with a sound like a slammed fist.
He has a bad knee that takes his balance when the world leans; I know because his steps are the kind you apologise for.
He was bitten on the forearm.

The bridge that had been the short cut was worse than pencil on paper — planks gone, beams splintered like someone had used the bridge for a kind of violence. Cars sat on the lip of the span, bumper to bumper, and a mound of wreckage had been heaped across the far side. A snapped support leaned like a broken finger.
The map's detour paperwork would toss us the rail yard. Dan pointed and said, "Rail yard's the only route left. Less cover, more noise — but it gets us past the bridge."

claims.quote: The pickup's battery is weak; I scraped the terminals, taped a cracked vacuum hose enough to keep the hand pump from wobbling, twisted a spare cable into a bypass and cranked the starter relay so she would spin smoother.
claims.value: battery weak; terminals cleaned; cracked vacuum hose taped; starter relay bypassed with spare cable
